## Summary

Shenzhen Gongjin Electronics, whose predecessor T&W was founded in 1991, dates itself from 1998, has been listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange A-share market (603118) since February 2015, and develops, manufactures and sells communication products including fibre access, Wi-Fi, switches, 5G fixed wireless and automotive electronics, with R&D and production bases in Shenzhen and elsewhere [3]. The IEEE registry lists 24 MA-L blocks to "SHENZHEN GONGJIN ELECTRONICS CO.,LT", at Songgang, Nanshan and Shekou addresses in Shenzhen and one in Shanghai, plus one MA-L block each to "SHENZHEN GONGJIN ELECTRONICS CO.,LTD" and "Shengzhen Gongjin Electronics" and one MA-M block to the latter, all three of those at Danzi North Road, Pingshan District, Shenzhen [1][2].

A MAC in a Gongjin block is most likely a home router, mesh node, extender or DSL or PON gateway sold under someone else's brand: WikiDevi says the company makes a large quantity of DSL modems for several major companies and lists Gongjin-built devices sold as ASUS, D-Link, Motorola, Netgear, eero, Nokia, DZS, TRENDnet, Zoom, ZyXEL and SmartRG [4]. The silicon follows the brand's design rather than the ODM's: MediaTek MT7620A and MT7610EN in the ASUS RT-AC51U, MediaTek MT7621AT with MT7905DAN in the Wi-Fi 6 RT-AX53U, Broadcom BCM6755 in the RT-AX56U v2, MediaTek MT7621AT with MT7615N in the D-Link DIR-867 and Motorola MR2600, and Qualcomm IPQ8062 with QCA9882 in the first eero [4]. Most of those devices carry the brand's own FCC grantee code (MSQ for ASUS, KA2 for D-Link, 2AEM4 for eero), and V4V is the prefix of the three FCC IDs WikiDevi lists under Gongjin's own name [4]. WikiDevi names PHY modes (802.11b/g/n, a/n/ac, ax) rather than bands in GHz, so no band is listed [4].

Parent company, randomization and security advisories are not documented by the sources consulted; NVD's search pages did not render for the session that wrote this entry, and advisories for these devices are filed under the brand on the box.
